sourceTitle: I have family with mobility issues visiting, what us there to do here that doesn't involve walking, standing, or sitting in a hot stadium?
author: Puzzleheaded-Food160
summary: A commenter described difficulty navigating the natural history museum, reporting keys needed for chairlifts and elevators they understood to be restricted to employees. They said getting around depended on knowing the layout.
caveat: One unverified community account; no visit date, specific lift, or route identified. This is not a finding that all elevators are restricted or that the entire museum is inaccessible. Confirm the intended route with visitor services.

sourceTitle: Exploring the Role of In-Gallery Technology-Based Interactives on Visitor-Object Experience
publisher: Kent State University / OhioLINK Electronic Theses and Dissertations Center
author: Haley N. Shaw
summary: In a visitor interview, an unnamed wheelchair user described limited views into elevated display cases. Images on the Antiquities Gallery touch table let her see objects from angles she could not see directly, improving her experience.
caveat: November 2019 thesis, printed page 35; exact publication day and visit date are unknown. This is one anonymized participant's account in a three-person study, not a current assessment of the gallery or confirmation the same interactive remains available.

sourceTitle: Winton Woods Campground — Liz C review
author: Liz C
summary: A camper described site 1R, identified in their review as an accessible site, as spacious, level, and concrete. They also enjoyed the paved pond-side walking trail connecting to the campground and found sites in the back loops less consistently level.
caveat: Specific campground observations from late winter and early spring 2022; exact visit dates unknown. The reviewer did not describe testing the site with a wheelchair. This does not establish restroom, transfer, or whole-park access.

sourceTitle: Miami Whitewater Forest Campground — Rkeller57 review
author: Rkeller57
summary: A first-time camper described a hilly campground with uneven gravel or dirt sites. They found entrance directions confusing and campsite numbers difficult to see because they were placed on hookups set back from the road.
caveat: A 2022 camper's observations, not a wheelchair-access audit; exact visit date unknown. The review lists site 136. These comments concern the campground, not the Shaker Trace Trail or every area of Miami Whitewater Forest.

summary: A parent visiting Adventure Station described an elevator to its upper play level and considered the play-shop area navigable by wheelchair. They found the lower level remained very dark during their visit and disclosed brightening their published photographs.
caveat: A 2019 family visit; exact visit date and individual author not established. Wheelchair use was not reported. This concerns Adventure Station in Sharonville, not every Sharon Woods facility or the different park near Columbus; present conditions may differ.
